# How to Find Family Time When December Is Already Full

By bedtime, you've reminded everyone about shoes, homework, dinner and whatever they need for school tomorrow. You've talked all day. Somehow, you haven't had time to hear what made anyone laugh.

December doesn't cancel work, school or laundry. It adds concerts, presents and the urgent discovery that tomorrow is Christmas jumper day. The jumper is, naturally, in the wash.

Coming up with a lovely family activity can feel like one more thing to remember. Having an idea ready makes that part a little easier.

## Start while the evening is still unfinished

Someone's clearing a plate. Someone else has claimed the comfortable end of the sofa. This can be the moment to ask, "Anyone fancy doing something together?" You can start with whoever wants to join. The rest of the evening can stay as it is.

**Before Christmas Slips By**, from Rise.Shine.Evolve. and The Happy Makers, is a family Advent calendar with 24 ready-to-use days. Each has a short pause, a game and a question to talk about, taking around ten minutes altogether.

Here are small glimpses from **three different days**.

### LET’S TAKE A MOMENT

**Empty Hands.** Put the phone, mug or tea towel somewhere safe. Rest your hands on your knees. For a minute, there's nothing to carry, clean or put away. When did your hands last have absolutely nothing to do?

### LET’S DO THIS TOGETHER

In the **Family Machine**, everyone adds a repeating movement and sound of their own. Soon the living room sounds like a factory nobody knows how to switch off. Part of the challenge is stopping all at once, without agreeing on a signal. Someone will probably still be going.

### LET’S TALK

**“Who’s done something helpful lately that almost nobody noticed?”**

Perhaps someone helped a younger sibling find a lost glove, or remembered the thing everyone else forgot. You might want to say, "Thanks for doing that. It helped." Or you might want to hear what someone else noticed. There's no compulsory round of speeches.

## Leave room for the evening you actually have

Five minutes may be enough tonight. Two people can use a two-person version of a game. If everyone needs a quiet evening on their own, skip a day; tomorrow won't come with a double session. The small **TRY IT TOMORROW** idea gives you a way to use a brief pause during an ordinary day, too.

There are no extra supplies to shop for or activities to set up beforehand. You get to sit down and join in, rather than spend the whole time getting things ready for everyone else.

The laundry will still be there afterwards. For a few minutes, you might have something else to talk about.

**BEFORE CHRISTMAS SLIPS BY. A BOOK THAT FITS INTO YOUR DECEMBER.**

**Take a look inside and find somewhere to begin.**

# An Activity Advent Calendar the Grown Ups Can Enjoy Too

The children are asleep. You remember tomorrow's Advent envelope is supposed to contain an activity. What activity? And do you have everything you need for it?

Some families love making their own calendars. If that's you, enjoy it. If you've reached December with plenty to do already, it's useful to have the ideas waiting on the page.

**Before Christmas Slips By**, from Rise.Shine.Evolve. and The Happy Makers, gives families 24 ready-to-use days of short pauses, games and conversation. About ten minutes a day, with no extra shopping or activity prep.

The grown-ups get a turn as well. You could be the one trying to guess what on earth everyone is acting out, instead of the one finding the scissors and explaining the rules for the third time.

## A look at the activities

Here are three short examples from **three different days**. They're a taste of the book, rather than a complete day's page.

### LET’S TAKE A MOMENT

**One Sound Quieter.** The TV is on. Notifications keep chiming. Someone's trying to tell a story. Turn down one source of noise you can control, such as the TV, for a minute. Listen to the room with a little less going on. Nobody has to become a quieter sort of person.

### LET’S DO THIS TOGETHER

**Reverse Charades.** One person guesses while the others quietly choose a shared prompt. Everyone else then acts it out at once, without speaking or agreeing on the gestures. With "building a snowman", three people may appear to be playing three different winter sports. That's part of the fun.

### LET’S TALK

**“What little things have we picked up from each other?”**

A phrase your mum says. A song your child got stuck in everyone's head. The way Grandad makes a sandwich. You can trace a small family habit back to whoever started it, including the person who insists they've never said that in their life.

## Ready for a weeknight

The games include **TWO PEOPLE** versions, so a smaller group can play too. **TRY IT TOMORROW** offers a small way to use that day's pause again. Some evenings you may want all three parts; on others, one will do.

You can skip a day without creating a backlog. Anyone can sit a game out. And whoever opens the book doesn't have to spend the evening running the entertainment.

Look through the activities with your own family in mind. Who would make charades unnecessarily complicated? Who would still be defending their extremely obvious snowman after the game had finished?

**A BOOK THAT FITS INTO YOUR DECEMBER.**

**Take a look inside Before Christmas Slips By and choose something to try together.**
